title: CENTCOM Declares Hormuz Shipping Lanes Cleared of Iranian Mines; Iran's Oil Exports at Zero Since Blockade Resumed
detail: CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper released a video message Thursday night (Aug 27) declaring international shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz fully cleared of Iranian-laid sea mines, saying divers, special operations personnel, and aircraft had 'meticulously and quietly' cleared the traffic separation scheme over several months: 'Today, international shipping lanes are open and momentum is building... The circumstances were challenging and dangerous, to say the least, but we got the job done.' CENTCOM said US forces have escorted nearly 1,500 commercial vessels carrying roughly 750 million barrels of crude through the strait since the blockade began, turned back about 75 vessels attempting to breach it, and disabled 3 non-compliant vessels. Iran has exported zero oil from its own shores since the naval blockade resumed in mid-July, per CENTCOM. Despite the mine-clearing claim, traffic remains far below pre-war levels — only about 10 commercial vessels transited Wednesday against a already-depressed 10-day average of 15, a fraction of the 20+ million bbl/day that transited before Feb 28. Trump separately expressed optimism Thursday about an imminent resolution, though talks between Washington and Tehran remain stalled.

confidenceReason: On-record CENTCOM commander statement with specific operational figures, corroborated by multiple Tier 2 outlets.

title: Iran Names Conditions for Reopening Hormuz, Calls US Sanctions 'Economic Terrorism' and Urges Global Pushback
detail: Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Iran is compiling a formal list of conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz after mediators asked Tehran to set them out, and confirmed Iran agreed to a temporary shipping corridor with Oman if the US meets Iran's terms: 'The US must first take practical steps to fulfil Iran's conditions, and then Iran will proceed to open the Strait of Hormuz.' An IRGC spokesperson told IRNA the conditions include an end to the regional war, lifting the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, compensation for war damages, and removal of sanctions, alongside implementation of the Iran-Oman corridor and joint mine-clearing project. Separately, Iran's Foreign Ministry issued a statement calling the newly launched 'Operation Economic Outcast' sanctions package 'an international crime and a crime against humanity' designed to 'inflict suffering on the Iranian people,' urging 'all countries' to refrain from implementing the measures and warning that compliance would amount to 'complicity in imposing one state's unlawful will on independent states.' President Trump reiterated he has 'no time schedule, none — I'm not in a hurry' to resume talks, and the White House said the US is focused on economic pressure rather than negotiations. CNBC characterized Iran's posture as calling for global pushback against the sanctions while signaling diplomacy 'isn't impossible.'
